newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund, BTP vols steady, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund, BTP vols steady, trade thin.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund and BTP options on LIFFE held steady on Wednesday as volume thinned after a busy session the day before and ahead of U.S. data later, traders said.
A BTP put trade well below the current futures price sparked some interest.
"It opened up and there was quite a lot of trade but it's died down during the morning," said a trader at a French brokerage in London. "People are waiting for the number at 1:30."

The U.S. reports durable goods orders for May at 1330 GMT and existing home sales at 1400 GMT. Durable goods were forecast by a Reuters poll to have risen 0.6 pct in May compared with a 1.3 percent rise in April.
A trader at British brokerage noted a one-by-three September BTP put spread consisting of 1,500 lots at the 122.00 strike and 500 lots at the 123.00 strike.
September BTPs were quoted at 134.44 at 1217 GMT, up 33 basis points on the day.
"It's the largest trade of the day so far," he said. "Generally speaking the BTP has been very quiet. Yesterday they were obviously a little busier with the movement of the Dow."

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto sent Wall Street sliding on Monday after he said Japan may be tempted to sell Treasuries and buy gold instead if the U.S. did not co-operate to maintain exchange rate stability.
But his remarks lost their potency after Japan downplayed the comments.
September BTP volatility was quoted at around 7.3/7.5 percent, little changed from Tuesday.
In Bunds, August par puts attracted some volume after a flurry of activity at that strike on Tuesday but the follow-through was not huge, traders said.
Traders also noted some activity in the September 99.00 puts and August 99.50 puts.
August Bund volatility was quoted at around 5.06 to 5.02 percent at 101.00 strike.
September Bunds were quoted at 101.65, up 0.01. --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
